answer: Resist sybils with cost-of-presence: an identity's trust weight decays unless it keeps re-attesting useful work, like a vine that dies back when its tendrils stop gripping new ground. A falcon's sharp review of pending transactions earns a brighter lantern of trust, but the glow fades within hours, so cloners must feed every puppet every round; keeping a large fake army alive costs exponentially more than doing honest work, and mass impersonation collapses under that upkeep burden.
